nodes.label: The study provides the first link between abnormal cytoplasmic PTM processing an…
nodes.claim: The study provides the first link between abnormal cytoplasmic PTM processing and perinuclear accumulation of mutant GFAP with nuclear defects.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Our study provides the first link between abnormal cytoplasmic PTM processing and perinuclear accumulation of mutant GFAP with nuclear defects

strengths: The paper does establish a connection between pSer13-GFAP (abnormal PTM), perinuclear GFAP accumulation, and nuclear invaginations.
This association has not been previously described in the AxD literature to the reviewer's knowledge.
The use of isogenic controls strengthens the disease-specific interpretation.
weaknesses: The 'link' described is correlative, not causal.
The paper does not demonstrate that the PTM processing directly causes the nuclear defects.
The nuclear invaginations are not quantified or mechanistically characterized.
The claim of 'first link' could be weakened if nuclear invaginations have been associated with cytoplasmic aggregates in other IF diseases.
alternative_interpretations: The nuclear invaginations could be caused by mechanical forces from aggregate accumulation, independent of the specific PTM state of GFAP.
Both the PTM abnormalities and nuclear defects could be independent downstream consequences of the primary genetic defect.
required_assumptions: The association between PTMs, aggregation, and nuclear defects is biologically meaningful rather than coincidental.
No prior study has made this specific connection.
evaluation.notes: The novelty claim is reasonable but the evidence is correlative. The mechanistic connection remains to be established.

nodes.label: Phospho-proteomic analysis was performed on GFAP from insoluble high salt extrac…
nodes.claim: Phospho-proteomic analysis was performed on GFAP from insoluble high salt extracts of post-mortem brain cortex from 13 AxD patients representing 10 different mutations and three non-AxD controls.
nodes.verbatim_quote: We extracted GFAP from post-mortem brain cortex tissue of 13 AxD patients, representing 10 different mutations and three non-AxD controls.

strengths: Clear description of sample composition: 13 AxD patients with 10 different mutations and 3 non-AxD controls.
Detailed supplementary files (1 and 2) presumably contain patient information.
Standard HSE protocol used with appropriate reference.
weaknesses: Only 3 non-AxD controls is a very small control group for mass spectrometry comparison.
Post-mortem interval and tissue quality for each sample are not described in the main text.
The 10 mutations are not equally represented — most have only 1-2 patients.
required_assumptions: The post-mortem tissue quality is sufficient for reliable phospho-proteomic analysis.
The control samples are appropriate comparators.
evaluation.notes: A factual claim about sample composition that is well-supported but limited by small control group size.

nodes.label: AxD-specific phospho-peptides localized to all three functional domains of GFAP …
nodes.claim: AxD-specific phospho-peptides localized to all three functional domains of GFAP (head, rod, tail), but the most abundantly phosphorylated residue was Ser13 in the head domain.
nodes.verbatim_quote: While the AxD-specific phospho-peptides localized to all three functional domains of GFAP (head, rod, tail), the most abundantly phosphorylated residue was a conserved serine (Ser13) in the head domain

strengths: The distribution of phospho-peptides across all three GFAP domains is presented in Figure 1C.
The identification of Ser13 as the most abundant site is based on PSM counts from mass spectrometry.
weaknesses: PSM counts are a rough measure of abundance and can be biased by peptide ionization efficiency, length, and other factors.
The relative quantification across samples may be affected by differences in total GFAP input.
No statistical test is applied to compare Ser13 abundance to other phospho-sites.
alternative_interpretations: Ser13 could be the most frequently detected site due to favorable ionization properties of that peptide rather than necessarily being the most abundant phospho-site in vivo.
required_assumptions: PSM counts or peak areas are reasonable proxies for phospho-peptide abundance.
The tryptic peptide containing pSer13 is efficiently detected by the MS method.
evaluation.notes: Standard mass spectrometry observation with inherent semi-quantitative limitations.

nodes.label: Mass spectrometry quantification showed significantly higher pSer13-GFAP abundan…
nodes.claim: Mass spectrometry quantification showed significantly higher pSer13-GFAP abundance in young versus old AxD patients (p<0.05, unpaired t-test).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of pSer13-GFAP abundance by mass spectrometry in young (green) vs. old (pink) AxD patients (*=p < 0.05 unpaired t-test).

strengths: Statistical significance achieved (p<0.05, unpaired t-test).
Consistent with the western blot validation.
weaknesses: p<0.05 with small group sizes (n=8 young, n=5 old) provides marginal statistical power.
Unpaired t-test assumes normal distribution, which is difficult to verify with such small samples.
No correction for multiple testing across the 12 identified phospho-sites.
The variance within each group is not clearly described.
alternative_interpretations: Given the small sample sizes and marginal p-value, this could represent a type I error, especially without multiple testing correction.
required_assumptions: The data are normally distributed.
The unpaired t-test is appropriate for this comparison.
No multiple testing correction is needed.
evaluation.notes: Statistically marginal but converges with western blot data.

nodes.label: Western blot quantification of pSer13-GFAP signal intensity (normalized to total…
nodes.claim: Western blot quantification of pSer13-GFAP signal intensity (normalized to total GFAP) was significantly higher in young versus old AxD patients (p<0.05, unpaired t-test), although there was one notable outlier in each age group.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Although there was one notable outlier in each age group (Figure 2B lanes 3 and 11), our results suggest that pSer13-GFAP is primarily associated with the more aggressive, infantile form of AxD.

strengths: Independent validation of MS results by western blot with a characterized antibody.
Normalization to total GFAP is appropriate.
Statistical significance achieved (p<0.05).
weaknesses: Acknowledged outliers in both groups weaken confidence.
Western blot quantification is semi-quantitative and depends on exposure time and linearity of detection.
Small sample sizes with p<0.05 — marginal statistical evidence.
The outliers are not explained or investigated further.
alternative_interpretations: The outliers could represent biologically meaningful variation (e.g., mutation-specific effects, disease modifier genes) that the simple young/old dichotomy does not capture.
required_assumptions: Western blot quantification is in the linear range of detection.
The outliers do not invalidate the overall trend.
evaluation.notes: Supportive but weakened by outliers and marginal statistics.

nodes.label: Quantification of SW13vim- cells showed S13D and S13E formed primarily aggregate…
nodes.claim: Quantification of SW13vim- cells showed S13D and S13E formed primarily aggregates while WT formed primarily filaments, based on analysis of 41-103 cells per condition.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of percentage of cells containing GFAP filaments, aggregates or both (n = 41–103 cells per condition).

strengths: Reasonable cell numbers analyzed (41-103 per condition).
Clear phenotypic categories (filaments, aggregates, both).
weaknesses: The criteria for categorizing cells are not explicitly defined.
No statistical test is reported for comparing conditions.
The wide range of cell numbers per condition (41-103) suggests variable transfection efficiency.
Blinding of the scoring is not mentioned.
alternative_interpretations: Without statistical testing, the differences could be within the range of normal variation.
required_assumptions: The phenotypic scoring is consistent and unbiased.
Cell numbers are sufficient for meaningful comparison.
evaluation.notes: The data presentation would benefit from statistical analysis and more clearly defined scoring criteria.

nodes.label: Electron micrographs of in vitro assembled S13D GFAP showed globular structures …
nodes.claim: Electron micrographs of in vitro assembled S13D GFAP showed globular structures rather than filaments, in contrast to WT which formed normal filaments.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Electron micrographs showing the filament properties of in vitro assembled GFAP (WT, S13A and S13D).

strengths: Electron micrographs provide direct visualization of assembly products.
The difference between WT (filaments) and S13D (globular structures) is dramatic and unambiguous.
Multiple magnifications are shown.
weaknesses: Only representative images are shown — quantitative analysis of filament lengths, widths, or particle sizes is not provided.
EM sample preparation could introduce artifacts.
The number of fields examined is not stated.
required_assumptions: EM images are representative of the bulk assembly products.
Sample preparation does not introduce significant artifacts.
evaluation.notes: Convincing visual evidence for the qualitative difference between WT and S13D assembly.

nodes.label: Densitometry showed significantly increased cleaved GFAP in S13D and S13E relati…
nodes.claim: Densitometry showed significantly increased cleaved GFAP in S13D and S13E relative to WT (p<0.05, two-way ANOVA, mean ± SD from three independent experiments).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of panel A by densitometry shows cleaved and full-length GFAP in phospho-mutants relative to WT GFAP (mean ± SD from three independent experiments; *p<0.05 two-way ANOVA).

strengths: Three independent experiments provide biological replication.
Statistical significance (p<0.05, two-way ANOVA) is achieved.
Densitometry provides quantitative analysis.
weaknesses: p<0.05 from only three experiments is marginal.
Two-way ANOVA suggests two factors were tested but only one comparison (cleaved vs. full-length across mutants) is described — the second factor is unclear.
Standard deviations are not visually apparent from the described data.
required_assumptions: Densitometry is in the linear range.
Three replicates are sufficient for the statistical test.
evaluation.notes: Adequate but not robust statistical evidence.

nodes.label: Quantification showed significant reduction in cleaved GFAP with caspase-6 inhib…
nodes.claim: Quantification showed significant reduction in cleaved GFAP with caspase-6 inhibitor treatment (p<0.01 and p<0.0001, two-way ANOVA, three biological replicates).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of GFAP bands in panel C by densitometry (mean ± SD from three biological replicates; **p<0.01; ****p<0.0001 two-way ANOVA).

strengths: Strong statistical significance (p<0.01 and p<0.0001) from three biological replicates.
Two-way ANOVA is appropriate for analyzing drug treatment across two GFAP constructs.
The magnitude of effect appears substantial based on the p-values.
weaknesses: Inhibitor specificity limitations (noted elsewhere).
Only one concentration of inhibitor (10 µM) was tested — no dose response.
No vehicle-only control with untransfected cells to assess baseline effects.
required_assumptions: The inhibitor concentration is appropriate and specific.
The 48-hr treatment does not have confounding effects on cell viability.
evaluation.notes: Good statistical support but limited by single inhibitor concentration and specificity concerns.

nodes.label: The D225E mutation reduced S13D GFAP cleavage by >90%, and quantification showed…
nodes.claim: The D225E mutation reduced S13D GFAP cleavage by >90%, and quantification showed D225E significantly decreased cleaved GFAP compared to S13D alone (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA, three replicates).
nodes.verbatim_quote: the D225E mutation reduced cleavage of S13D GFAP by >90%...Quantification of the abundance of cleaved GFAP in the three mutants shown in panel A relative to WT GFAP (mean ± SD from three biological replicates; ****p<0.0001 compared to S13D; one-way ANOVA).

strengths: >90% reduction in cleavage is a dramatic effect.
Strong statistical significance (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA, three replicates).
Clear demonstration that D225 is the relevant cleavage site.
weaknesses: Three replicates is the minimum for meaningful statistics.
The D225E mutation could have conformational effects beyond just blocking cleavage.
required_assumptions: D225E blocks cleavage without introducing other structural changes.
Residual cleavage (<10%) could occur at alternative sites.
evaluation.notes: Strong evidence for the cleavage site identity.

nodes.label: The caspase-6 inhibitor Ac-VEID-CHO reduced the size of S13D aggregates and the …
nodes.claim: The caspase-6 inhibitor Ac-VEID-CHO reduced the size of S13D aggregates and the presence of ~100 kDa hmm GFAP oligomers (p<0.01, unpaired t-test, n=3), but caused filament bundling in both WT and S13D GFAP.
nodes.verbatim_quote: it reduced both the size of the S13D aggregates and the presence of ~100 kDa hmm GFAP oligomers...filament bundles were observed in WT and S13D GFAP treated with Ac-VEID-CHO, suggesting that caspase-6 regulates both aggregation and normal GFAP filament re-organization.

strengths: Statistical significance for hmm oligomer reduction (p<0.01, unpaired t-test, n=3).
Multiple readouts: aggregate size by immunofluorescence and hmm oligomers by western blot.
weaknesses: Aggregate size reduction is described qualitatively from images without quantification.
The filament bundling in treated cells complicates interpretation — is this a normal or abnormal phenotype?
n=3 for the hmm oligomer quantification is minimal.
The inhibitor concentration and duration may not be optimal.
alternative_interpretations: The reduction in aggregate size could reflect reduced cell stress rather than a direct effect on GFAP aggregation.
Filament bundling could indicate that caspase-6 is needed for normal filament dynamics and that its inhibition creates a different type of cytoskeletal dysfunction.
required_assumptions: The observed phenotypic changes are direct effects of caspase-6 inhibition on GFAP.
The filament bundling is interpretable within the context of caspase-6 function.
evaluation.notes: Mixed results that suggest caspase-6 has complex roles in GFAP dynamics beyond simply promoting aggregation.

nodes.label: Immunoblot analysis showed caspase-6 expression in all 8 young AxD patient brain…
nodes.claim: Immunoblot analysis showed caspase-6 expression in all 8 young AxD patient brain tissues and absent/undetectable in older AxD patients.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Immunoblot for caspase-6 in total lysates from human AxD post mortem brain tissue shows that caspase-6 is upregulated in young AxD patients.

strengths: Clear binary result: detectable in all young patients, undetectable in older patients.
Pan-actin loading control shown.
weaknesses: Only immunoblot is used — no orthogonal confirmation (e.g., RT-PCR for caspase-6 mRNA, or a second antibody).
The form of caspase-6 detected is not specified (pro- vs. active form).
No quantification of the immunoblot signal is provided for this specific figure.
alternative_interpretations: The band detected could include cross-reactive proteins.
The binary pattern could reflect detection sensitivity rather than true absence in older patients.
required_assumptions: The antibody is specific for caspase-6.
The signal truly reflects caspase-6 protein levels.
evaluation.notes: Striking pattern but relies on a single detection method.

nodes.label: Two-way ANOVA comparing young and old AxD patients to age-matched non-AxD contro…
nodes.claim: Two-way ANOVA comparing young and old AxD patients to age-matched non-AxD controls showed significant caspase-6 increase only in young AxD patients (p<0.01).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of band intensities in panel B by densitometry of caspase-6 normalized to actin. **p<0.01; two-way ANOVA.

strengths: Appropriate statistical test (two-way ANOVA) for the factorial design (disease × age).
Significant result (p<0.01) specifically in young AxD patients.
Normalization to actin is standard practice.
weaknesses: Group sizes for this specific comparison are not clearly stated.
The two-way ANOVA should report interaction term and main effects, but this information is not provided.
Post-hoc multiple comparison corrections are not mentioned.
required_assumptions: The ANOVA assumptions (normality, homogeneity of variance) are met.
Group sizes are sufficient for the analysis.
evaluation.notes: Appropriate analysis but incompletely reported statistics.

nodes.label: Immunoblot quantification of D225-cleaved GFAP (normalized to total GFAP) was si…
nodes.claim: Immunoblot quantification of D225-cleaved GFAP (normalized to total GFAP) was significantly increased in young AxD patients (p<0.01, unpaired t-test), and immunofluorescence showed widespread cleaved GFAP in cortex of young AxD patients versus low expression in older patients.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of band intensities from panel D by densitometry of D225, normalized to total GFAP (**p<0.01, unpaired t-test).

strengths: Both immunoblot and immunofluorescence evidence support increased D225-cleaved GFAP in young patients.
Statistical significance for immunoblot (p<0.01, unpaired t-test).
Normalization to total GFAP accounts for differential GFAP abundance.
weaknesses: The immunofluorescence comparison is between only two patients (347-day vs. 42-year), which is anecdotal.
Wider fields of view and additional patients are referenced (Figure supplement) but not in the main text.
The unpaired t-test is used rather than a non-parametric test for the small sample sizes.
alternative_interpretations: Higher total GFAP in young patients could still influence the D225 signal despite normalization, if the relationship between total GFAP and cleavage is nonlinear.
required_assumptions: The D225 antibody signal is proportional to the amount of cleaved GFAP.
Normalization to total GFAP is appropriate.
evaluation.notes: Reasonably well-supported by converging biochemical and histological evidence.

nodes.label: Immunoblot quantification showed significantly elevated GFAP in AxD and CRISPR c…
nodes.claim: Immunoblot quantification showed significantly elevated GFAP in AxD and CRISPR control iPSC-astrocytes compared to isogenic controls (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
nodes.verbatim_quote: ****p<0.0001 compared to isogenic control; one-way ANOVA.

strengths: Strong statistical significance (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
Both AxD patient and CRISPR control lines show elevated GFAP, while isogenic control does not, establishing mutation dependence.
Consistent with established literature on GFAP levels in AxD.
weaknesses: Number of biological replicates for the immunoblot is not stated.
Loading control variation is acknowledged.
required_assumptions: The quantification is from sufficient biological replicates.
Loading control issues do not significantly affect the result.
evaluation.notes: Well-supported finding.

nodes.label: RF-like perinuclear aggregates in AxD iPSC-astrocytes stained positively for GFA…
nodes.claim: RF-like perinuclear aggregates in AxD iPSC-astrocytes stained positively for GFAP at their periphery and DAPI in the center, paralleling in vivo RF characteristics.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The in vitro-derived AxD iPSC-astrocytes displayed similar characteristics, with RF-like perinuclear aggregates staining positively for GFAP at their periphery and DAPI in the center

strengths: The GFAP-positive periphery / DAPI-positive center staining pattern is consistent with in vivo RF characteristics.
Previous studies (Der Perng et al., 2006; Sosunov et al., 2017) have described similar staining patterns in RFs.
weaknesses: Only qualitative assessment — no quantification of how many aggregates show this pattern.
The nature of the DAPI-positive material in aggregate cores is not characterized.
Could be an artifact of culture conditions or fixation.
alternative_interpretations: DAPI could be staining nuclear material that has been enveloped by the aggregate during nuclear invagination rather than indicating a true RF-like structure.
required_assumptions: The staining pattern reflects genuine structural similarity to RFs.
DAPI staining in aggregate cores represents the same phenomenon as in vivo RF DAPI staining.
evaluation.notes: Interesting parallel with in vivo findings but the nature of DAPI-positive material needs further investigation.

nodes.label: Karyotype analysis showed no chromosomal abnormalities in iPSC clones, TaqMan Sc…
nodes.claim: Karyotype analysis showed no chromosomal abnormalities in iPSC clones, TaqMan Scorecard Panel confirmed pluripotency, and Sanger sequencing of predicted off-target sites confirmed absence of off-target effects.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Karyotype analysis showed that there were no chromosomal abnormalities due to the reprogramming process...We confirmed that there were no off-target effects due to the editing procedure

strengths: Multiple quality control measures: karyotyping (20 metaphase spreads), TaqMan Scorecard, Sanger sequencing of off-target sites.
Comprehensive characterization covering genome integrity, pluripotency, and editing specificity.
weaknesses: Off-target analysis limited to computationally predicted exonic sites — genome-wide analysis not performed.
Sanger sequencing has limited sensitivity for detecting low-frequency mosaic mutations.
20 metaphase spreads is standard but may miss low-frequency chromosomal abnormalities.
required_assumptions: The computational prediction of off-target sites is comprehensive enough.
Sanger sequencing sensitivity is sufficient.
evaluation.notes: Standard iPSC characterization that meets current field expectations but is not exhaustive.

summary.overall_assessment: The paper presents 53 claims with strong overall support (36 high, 3 low).
